```rust
extern crate faccess
```

---

`faccess` provides an extension trait for `std::path::Path` which adds an
[`access`](https://docs.rs/faccess/0.2.4/faccess/trait.PathExt.html#tymethod.access) method for checking the accessibility of a path for the given access
permissions — a bitwise-inclusive OR of one or more [`AccessMode`](https://docs.rs/faccess/0.2.4/faccess/struct.AccessMode.html) flags
(`EXISTS`, `READ`, `WRITE`, `EXECUTE`).

It also provides convenience methods [`readable`](https://docs.rs/faccess/0.2.4/faccess/trait.PathExt.html#method.readable), [`writable`](https://docs.rs/faccess/0.2.4/faccess/trait.PathExt.html#method.writable), and [`executable`](https://docs.rs/faccess/0.2.4/faccess/trait.PathExt.html#method.executable)
if only a single permission needs to be checked in a simple boolean fashion.

# Example

```rust
use std::path::Path;
use faccess::{AccessMode, PathExt};

let path = Path::new("/bin/ls");

assert!(path.access(AccessMode::READ | AccessMode::EXECUTE).is_ok());
assert!(path.readable());
assert!(!path.writable());
assert!(path.executable());
```

# Platform-specific Behaviour

On Unix platforms, `access` directly maps to [`faccessat(2)`](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/functions/access.html), with the
`AT_EACCESS` flag used where available to test against the effective user and
group ID's.

On Windows, a complex custom implementation is used to approximate these
semantics in a best-effort fashion, using a mixture of file extension checks,
simply attempting to open a file, [`GetNamedSecurityInfoW`](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/aclapi/nf-aclapi-getnamedsecurityinfow), and [`AccessCheck`](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/securitybaseapi/nf-securitybaseapi-accesscheck),
depending on the permissions being checked.  This is similar to implementations
found in other languages.

On other platforms it simply proxies to `exists()` and `readonly()` as appropriate.

# Caveats

There is a history of time-of-check to time-of-use ([TOCTOU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time-of-check_to_time-of-use)) bugs with this
class of function, particularly with set-user-ID programs relying on them to
validate effective user/group permissions prior to accessing files on behalf
of other users.  They should not be relied upon in a security context.

```rust
pub fn is_dir(&self) -> bool
```

---

Tests whether this file type represents a directory. The
result is mutually exclusive to the results of
[`is_file`] and [`is_symlink`]; only zero or one of these
tests may pass.

# Examples

```rust
fn main() -> std::io::Result<()> {
    use std::fs;

    let metadata = fs::metadata("foo.txt")?;
    let file_type = metadata.file_type();

    assert_eq!(file_type.is_dir(), false);
    Ok(())
}
```

[`is_file`]: https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/std/fs/struct.FileType.html#method.is_file

```rust
pub fn executable(&self) -> bool
```

---

`Self` = `Path`

---

Returns `true` if the path points at an executable entity.

Equivalent to [`access(AccessMode::EXECUTE).is_ok()`](https://docs.rs/faccess/0.2.4/faccess/trait.PathExt.html#tymethod.access).

# Examples

```rust
use std::path::Path;
use faccess::PathExt;

assert_eq!(Path::new("/bin/ls").executable(), true);
```

```rust
impl<T> Option<T>
pub const fn unwrap_or_default(self) -> T
where
    T: Default,
```

---

`T` = `Style`

---

Returns the contained [`Some`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.Some) value or a default.

Consumes the `self` argument then, if [`Some`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.Some), returns the contained
value, otherwise if [`None`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None), returns the [default value] for that
type.

# Examples

```rust
let x: Option<u32> = None;
let y: Option<u32> = Some(12);

assert_eq!(x.unwrap_or_default(), 0);
assert_eq!(y.unwrap_or_default(), 12);
```

[default value]: https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/core/default/trait.Default.html#tymethod.default
